text: Yeah exactly right and i would also make sure that the texture scales, and isnt defaulted to a size. since if u for example u make a big ass bridge, u dont want to stretch that one 512 texture across a huge surface though, i guess making a bridge is probably best done in parts
resolution: Evolved paint_texture_demo to tile the material at a WORLD scale instead of a default. final = material(in.uv * tilesAcross) * paintMask(cell), where tilesAcross = surfaceMetres / tileMetres. So the texture's density is a physical metres-per-tile control (default 1 m/tile), and the two wrong defaults are exposed as the ends of one scale axis: 'Stretched' (tilesAcross=1 — one 512 tile smeared over the whole surface; a huge bridge gets one giant brick) and 'Per-cell' (tilesAcross=CELLS — one tile per paint cell). Material chips (Brick/Grass), scale chips (Stretched / 2 / 1 / 0.5 m per tile / Per-cell), surface chips (4/8/16 m) with a live 'N tiles across' readout. Verified with a seeded painted strip: at a fixed 1 m/tile, 4 m surface = 4 tiles (big bricks) and 16 m surface = 16 tiles (a proper brick wall) — bricks stay the same world size, only the count scales, proving no stretch. Also surfaced the user's point that a big bridge is best authored in PARTS: each part is one manageable surface carrying its own world-scaled material. No host/material-catalog code changed yet — this is the demo/blueprint; the real materials.ts shaders would gain a worldPerTile (or texels-per-metre) param consumed the same way.
